entries.comparison: Basic proves the barycenter sum-of-squares identity and translation-invariance equivalence. For the asserted converse, two-point centered configurations imply V(m+u)+V(m-u)=2V(m)+V(u)+V(-u)-2V(0). Differentiate twice in u at zero to make V second derivative constant, integrate twice to get a quadratic, use integrability to force positive quadratic coefficient, and use mass one to obtain the exact normalized Gaussian. The written barycenter calculation agrees. For Gaussian uniqueness the prose supplies the characterization claim but not a proof method, so the differentiating-two-point argument is an explicit expansion, not a claim to have checked an unwritten author proof. Smoothness is represented by C2, a weaker regularity premise than smoothness.
